thread:
jess (Support): FYI escalation from Acme - they see p99 latency jump starting ~2026-03-14T18:02Z after the routing change. Ticket T-4921 attached: https://redwood.at/t/T-4921. They say API returns 200 usually but observed a cluster of 504/timeout-like behavior and a big p99 spike on the 'API -> text.generate p99' panel.

mike (Oncall): @jess can you paste the grafana query + the sample request they used? also any request ids from the logs?

jess (Support): grafana panel: uses datasource 'prometheus-rollups', query was (copied from panel):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
```
sample curl they sent (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"model":"gpt-xl-1","inputs":"hello"}' -v
```
request ids seen in support logs: rID: 1a2b3c4d (multiple)

sara (SRE): thanks. quick thought: that query is fine for raw histograms, but our 'prometheus-rollups' datasource recently switched the bucket boundaries to the new 'auto-extend' config last week (2026-03-14 02:00 UTC) to support longer tails for batch workloads. If the rollup changed le boundaries, histogram_quantile on rollups can move percentiles unexpectedly.

anna (Observability): confirm - the rollup pipeline now normalizes to a common set of buckets per-aggregation-window. before we had 50ms buckets up to 1s, now we have extended buckets (doubling the top 'le' to 2s) for several routes. that makes the 0.99 quantile jump in dashboards even if raw samples are similar.

mike (Oncall): ok does raw prometheus (raw-ingest) show the same p99 delta? can we compare?

anna (Observability): doing side-by-side. raw-ingest query (prometheus-main):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",job="ingest"}[5m])) by (le))
```
raw shows a smaller bump (p99 ~420ms -> 520ms), rollup datasource shows ~420ms -> 980ms. so rollup exaggerates it.

sara (SRE): that matches a bucket-boundary drift. root cause hypothesis: the rollup's bucket re-binning changed the distribution mapping; for tail-heavy traffic small mass beyond old top-le reassigns to the new top bucket and histogram_quantile produces a larger quantile value.

rami (Product): how customer-impacting is this? the ticket says timeouts and 504s — is that a separate thing or just a dashboard artifact?

mike (Oncall): we saw increased 504 rate in the logs for the same timeframe for a subset of requests (same request id pattern). Not all requests timed out. Could be capacity/backpressure + the rollup made it look worse. we need to check retries and upstream 504 sources.

jess (Support): customer is pushing for workaround now, they want a clear explanation + mitigation.

sara (SRE): short-term mitigation options:
- revert rollup bucket change for affected routes (fast but touches infra)
- change dashboards to use raw-ingest panels for latency percentiles (editor change)
- change panel to use 'le'-aware smoothing query: use histogram_quantile with a larger window or use summary metrics if available
- operational mitigation: temporarily route their traffic to dedicated capacity (if customer on Dedicated) or reduce concurrency/raise request timeouts client-side

anna (Observability): pragmatic step 1: update the public dashboard for the customer-facing API to source from 'prometheus-main/ingest' for the p95/p99 panels and add a note: 'Note: rollup buckets migrated 2026-03-14; use ingest for accurate tail percentiles'. I'll open a PR to Grafana.

sara (SRE): step 2: we'll roll back the rollup bucket change for routes tagged 'api' in the next maintenance window unless we confirm the mixed rollup config is what we want. i'll put up an RFC to standardize bucket shape.

mike (Oncall): immediate customer-facing action: @jess can you message Acme: "we identified a metric re-binning in our rollup layer that's inflating p99 on dashboard. We're switching the dashboard to raw-ingest and investigating a config rollback. Meanwhile we see a small increase in 504s for a subset of requests; we're tracing those and will update in 30m." add support ticket link. :thumbsup:

jess (Support): sending now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: observability/grafana: patch/ingest-panels-for-p99 (deploy id d-7781)

mike (Oncall): noted a bit more: for reproducible triage, here's a quick query pair we used to compare in the future:
```
# rollup datasource (may lie after re-binning)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))

# raw-ingest datasource (prefer for tail accuracy)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",job="ingest"}[5m])) by (le))
```

anna (Observability): PR merged + grafana deploy in progress. adding a note to the dashboard and linking the ticket.

sara (SRE): action items assigned:
- anna: revert dashboard panels to ingest (done in PR) + add note (in PR)
- sara: rollup config RFC and rollback plan (I will own)
- mike: follow up on 504 origin (investigating backend queues and proxy timeouts)
- jess: customer communication (sent)

jess (Support): customer replied: "thanks, seeing panel update. still seeing occasional 504s but less frequent. appreciate the quick fix!" :relieved:

mike (Oncall): will keep monitoring for 2 hours and post an update. if 504 rate > 0.5% we'll escalate to infra and consider routing change.

sara (SRE): final note for the thread: dashboards that depend on rollup histograms are brittle when bucket sets change. prefer raw-ingest for SLA-facing panels or use summaries. we'll document.

(ends)
